newsitem.title: USA: BPA non-firm peak power for Tues up $1.50/MWh.
newsitem.headline: BPA non-firm peak power for Tues up $1.50/MWh.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) raised prices for firm power during peak demand hours on Tuesday, but did not offer any non-firm power during morning and evening peaks, the agency said Monday.
The agency also refrained from offering any displacement power for Tuesday, compared with recent offers as low as $5.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) for Northwest buyers.
BPA offered up to 300 megawatts of firm peak power on Tuesday at $12.50 per MWh for Northwest deliveries and $13.50 for California-Oregon border (COB), both up $1.50 from Monday.
Prices for firm and non-firm power during off-peak hours on Tuesday were unchanged at $9.00 per MWh for all deliveries.
Non-firm shoulder hour (0700, 1100-1700 and 2100-2300 PST) offers for Tuesday were up 50 cents at at $10.50 for Northwest and $11.50 for COB.
